parsed.rationale: Both records are unnamed extensions on (presumably) `UserDefaults` within the same `Caching` package, living in two separate files — `UserDefaults+WXYC.swift` (line 15) and `DefaultsStorage.swift` (line 47). Having two extension declarations on the same type in the same package without a clear separation-of-concern boundary creates a name-collision risk and makes it harder to reason about the full surface area of the extension. Since both records share the same package (`Caching`), carry no restraint markers, and the structural signal is `name-collisions`, consolidating them into a single canonical file (`UserDefaults+WXYC.swift`, which already carries the WXYC namespace convention) is the idiomatic Swift resolution. Any members from `DefaultsStorage.swift` that are logically distinct could be kept in a separate extension block within the same file, clearly delimited by a `// MARK:`.
